coordination_note: Some primary-source reads began while the atomic claim law landed concurrently. No new Trigger-6 result was persisted before the canonical F2 create-only claim succeeded; synthesis and result persistence occurred after the claim.

architecture_frontier.question: Which minimal mechanisms best bind canonical semantic effect-request bytes/digest, immutable invocation/event identity, idempotency, append-only outcome state, and explicit ambiguous UNKNOWN handling without importing a second effect authority or truth store?

source_level_findings: Idempotency keys may be derived from a hash of the entire payload or selected payload fields.
A separate validation hash can detect payload mutation under the same idempotency identity.
The persistence model distinguishes INPROGRESS, COMPLETE and expiry-related states and uses conditional persistence for concurrency control.
The exact current develop head fixes a Redis path where missing in_progress_expiry_timestamp caused a live INPROGRESS record to be reclaimed as an orphan, enabling concurrent double execution.
retain: semantic payload digest distinct from transport identity
fail-closed treatment of live/indeterminate INPROGRESS records
reject_or_modify: Do not copy timeout-expiry re-execution semantics onto post-dispatch real effects: an expired/unknown attempt may already have changed the world.
Do not add DynamoDB/Redis as a second F2 authority store.

source_level_findings: CloudEvents requires producer uniqueness for source+id and permits duplicate re-sends to retain the same id.
The spec distinguishes an occurrence from the event data structure describing it; one occurrence may result in more than one event.
The primer explicitly warns that event id is for uniqueness/deduplication and should not be overloaded with unrelated semantic meaning.
retain: separate occurrence/causal identity from concrete event/admission identity
source-scoped immutable event id for replay/deduplication
do not overload one id to mean semantic request, execution attempt and observed effect simultaneously
reject_or_modify: CloudEvents does not itself provide semantic request canonicalization, effect authorization, append-only outcome truth, or exactly-once external effects.

source_level_findings: Restate gives invocations unique IDs and supports caller-supplied idempotency keys with retained results.
Its durable-execution model journals operations/results and replays around completed work after crashes.
Its attach/output model permits querying an existing invocation rather than blindly dispatching a new one.
External-event primitives use unique completion IDs and durable waiting rather than assuming immediate completion.
retain: VERIFY_OR_ATTACH_TO_EXISTING_ATTEMPT before any replay of an ambiguous post-start action
separate invocation identity from idempotency identity
durable explicit waiting/unknown state until outcome evidence arrives
reject_or_modify: A Restate server/runtime/journal would introduce a large second durable execution authority next to UnifiedDB/EffectJournal.
Exactly-once or durable-platform claims cannot substitute for F2-specific effect verification evidence.

internal_reuse_observation.finding: The Research-Entity archive already contains exact RFC8785/JCS canonicalization work and fail-closed canonicalization receipts. The highest-value F2 path is therefore likely to reuse/distill that method for semantic effect-request bytes rather than add another canonicalization dependency.
internal_reuse_observation.boundary: Historical/component EntityOS JCS evidence is donor evidence only; F2-WP-105 receives no runtime or architecture credit until exact F2 source/tests bind the semantic effect request at its own current identity.

generated_minimal_contract_candidate.critical_rule: UNKNOWN_POST_DISPATCH is non-replayable by default. The next action is VERIFY/ATTACH/QUERY using the original attempt identity; replay is allowed only when the target effect has an independently proven stable idempotency contract or a newer explicit authority closes the uncertainty.

ranking: 1 AWS Powertools idempotency pattern: strongest small concurrency/idempotency donor, especially its current fail-closed bug lesson.
2 CloudEvents identity envelope: strongest thin donor for separating occurrence/event/replay identities.
3 Restate durable invocation: strongest donor for attach/query-after-ambiguity, but direct runtime adoption is architecture-hostile for F2.
counterhypothesis: A minimal F2-native JCS+SHA256 semantic-request binder plus existing EffectJournal transitions may outperform every external dependency; external systems may add more state ownership and failure modes than information or correctness.
next_discriminator: Trigger-6 should claim E2 only for the smallest structural packet: map the proposed semantic_request_sha256 + invocation_id + attempt_id + append-only outcome transition ABI onto exact current F2-WP-105 source and identify whether any existing F2/EntityOS primitive already satisfies each field. Do not run real effects and do not import Restate/AWS storage.
